verses.text: E happen say, while Apollos dey Corinth, Paul, as e don pass through di upper country, come reach Ephesus, find some disciples.
E talk to dem say, “Una receive Holy Spirit when una believe?” Dem talk to am say, “No, we never even hear say Holy Spirit dey.”
E talk say, “Den na wetin dem baptize una into?” Dem talk say, “Into John baptism.”
Paul talk say, “John baptize with di baptism of repentance, dey talk to di people say make dem believe di one wey go come after am, wey be Jesus.”
When dem hear this, dem baptize dem for di name of Lord Jesus.
When Paul put hands on dem, Holy Spirit come on dem, and dem talk other languages and prophesy.
Dem be about 12 men for all.
E enter di synagogue, talk boldly for three months, dey reason and persuade about God Kingdom.
But when some harden and disobey, dey talk evil about di Way before di crowd, e leave dem and separate di disciples, dey reason every day for Tyrannus school.
This continue for two years, so that all di people wey dey live for Asia hear di word of Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
God dey do special miracles by di hands of Paul,
so that even handkerchiefs or aprons dem carry from im body go give di sick, and di diseases leave dem, and di evil spirits go out.
But some of di Jews wey dey travel round, exorcists, take am on demself to call di name of Lord Jesus over di people wey get evil spirits, dey talk say, “I command una by Jesus wey Paul dey preach.”
Seven sons of one Sceva, Jewish chief priest, dey do this.
Di evil spirit answer, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who be una?”
Di man wey di evil spirit dey inside jump on dem, overpower dem, and win dem, so that dem run out of that house naked and wounded.
This become known to all, both Jews and Greeks, wey dey live for Ephesus. Fear catch dem all, and dem praise di name of Lord Jesus.
Many of di people wey don believe come too, dey confess, and dey declare dem deeds.
Many of di people wey practice magical arts bring dem books together burn dem before all. Dem count di price of dem, and find say e be 50,000 pieces of silver.
So di word of di Lord dey grow and dey become mighty.
Now after these things don finish, Paul decide for im spirit, when e don pass through Macedonia and Achaia, to go Jerusalem, dey talk say, “After I don dey there, I must see Rome too.”
As e don send two of di people wey dey serve am go Macedonia, Timothy and Erastus, e imself stay for Asia for some time.
About that time no small disturbance rise about di Way.
Because one man wey im name na Demetrius, silversmith, wey dey make silver shrines of Diana, dey bring no small business to di craftsmen;
wey e gather together, with di workmen of di same work, talk say, “Oga dem, una know say na by this business we get our wealth.
Una see and hear, say no be for Ephesus alone, but almost through all Asia, this Paul don persuade and turn away many people, dey talk say di things wey dem make with hands no be gods.
No be only say danger dey say our trade go lose respect, but say di temple of di great goddess Diana go count as nothing, and im majesty go destroy, wey all Asia and di world dey worship.”
When dem hear this, anger full dem, and dem shout, dey talk say, “Great na Diana of di Ephesians!”
Di whole city full with confusion, and dem rush with one mind enter di theater, as dem don catch Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul travel companions.
When Paul want enter go meet di people, di disciples no allow am.
Some of di Asiarchs too, wey be im friends, send to am beg am make e no risk enter di theater.
So some dey shout one thing, and some another, because di assembly dey confusion. Most of dem no know why dem gather.
Dem bring Alexander out of di crowd, di Jews dey push am forward. Alexander wave hand, and e wan make defense to di people.
But when dem know say e be Jew, all with one voice for about two hours shout, “Great na Diana of di Ephesians!”

When di town clerk don quiet di crowd, e talk say, “Una men of Ephesus, which man dey wey no know say di city of di Ephesians na temple keeper of di great goddess Diana, and of di image wey fall down from Jupiter?
As these things no fit dey denied, una suppose keep quiet, and no do anything rash.
Because una don bring these men here wey no be robbers of temples or blasphemers of una goddess.
So if Demetrius and di craftsmen wey dey with am get matter against anybody, di courts dey open and proconsuls dey. Make dem press charges against each other.
But if una dey look for anything about other matters, dem go settle am for di regular assembly.
Because truly we dey danger to dem accuse us of rioting about today, as no reason dey. About am, we no go fit give account of this commotion.”
When e don talk this, e dismiss di assembly.
After di uproar don stop, Paul send for di disciples, take leave of dem, and leave to go Macedonia.
When e don pass through those parts, and don encourage dem with many words, e come reach Greece.
When e don spend three months there, and Jews make plot against am as e dey about to sail go Syria, e decide to return through Macedonia.
These ones go with am reach Asia: Sopater of Beroea; Aristarchus and Secundus of di Thessalonians; Gaius of Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.
But these ones don go ahead, dey wait for us for Troas.
We sail from Philippi after di days of unleavened bread, come meet dem for Troas for five days, wia we stay seven days.
For di first day of di week, when di disciples gather together to break bread, Paul talk with dem, as e wan leave di next day, and e continue im speech until midnight.
Many lights dey for di upper room wia we gather together.

One young man wey im name na Eutychus dey sit for di window, deep sleep dey weigh am down. As Paul dey talk for longer time, as im sleep dey weigh am down, e fall from di third floor, and dem carry am up dead.
Paul go down, fall on am, hold am talk say, “No trouble, because im life dey inside am.”
When e don go up, break bread, chop, and talk with dem for long time, even until day break, e leave.
Dem bring di boy enter alive, and dem comfort no small.
But we wey go ahead to di ship sail go Assos, dey plan to take Paul for there, because e arrange am so, as e imself want go by land.
When e meet us for Assos, we take am enter di ship, come Mitylene.
As we sail from there, we come di next day opposite Chios. Di next day we touch Samos and stay for Trogyllium, and di day after we come Miletus.
Because Paul don decide to sail pass Ephesus, so that e no go spend time for Asia; because e dey hurry, if e possible, to dey Jerusalem for di day of Pentecost.
From Miletus e send to Ephesus, call di elders of di assembly to imself.
When dem come to am, e talk to dem say, “Una know yourselves, from di first day wey I set foot for Asia, how I dey with una all di time,
dey serve di Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials wey happen to me by di plots of di Jews;
how I no hold back from declaring to una anything wey profitable, dey teach una publicly and from house to house,
dey testify both to Jews and to Greeks repentance towards God, and faith towards our Lord Jesus Christ.
Now, look, I dey go bound by di Spirit to Jerusalem, no know wetin go happen to me there;
except say Holy Spirit dey testify for every city, dey talk say bonds and afflictions dey wait for me.

But these things no count; and I no hold my life dear to myself, so that I go finish my race with joy, and di ministry wey I receive from Lord Jesus, to fully testify to di Good News of di grace of God.
Now, look, I know say una all, among wey I go about dey preach God Kingdom, no go see my face again.
So I testify to una today say I clean from di blood of all men,
because I no hold back from declaring to una God whole plan.
So take care of yourselves, and all di flock, wey Holy Spirit don make una overseers over, to shepherd di assembly of Lord and God wey e buy with im own blood.
Because I know say after I leave, vicious wolves go enter among una, no go spare di flock.
Men go rise from among una own selves, dey talk perverse things, to draw di disciples go after dem.
So watch, remember say for three years I no stop to warn everybody night and day with tears.
Now, brothers, I commit una to God and to di word of im grace, wey fit build una up, and give una di inheritance among all di people wey dem make holy.
I no want anybody silver, or gold, or clothing.
Una know yourselves say these hands serve my needs, and di needs of di people wey dey with me.
For all things I give una example, say as una dey work so, una suppose help di weak, and remember di words of Lord Jesus, wey e imself talk, ‘E more blessed to give than to receive.’”
When e don talk these things, e kneel down pray with dem all.
Dem all cry plenty, fall on Paul neck, kiss am,
dey sorrow most because of di word wey e talk, say dem no go see im face again. And dem follow am go di ship.
E happen say as we don separate from dem and sail, we go straight reach Cos, and di next day Rhodes, and from there Patara.
As we find one ship wey dey cross to Phoenicia, we enter, sail.
When we come see Cyprus, leave am for di left hand, we sail to Syria, land for Tyre, because di ship go unload im cargo there.
As we find disciples, we stay there seven days. These ones talk to Paul through di Spirit say make e no go up to Jerusalem.
When we don finish di days, we leave go on our journey. Dem all, with wives and pikin dem, follow us for di way until we out of di city. We kneel down for di beach pray.
When we don say goodbye to each other, we enter di ship, and dem return home again.
When we don finish di voyage from Tyre, we reach Ptolemais. We greet di brothers, stay with dem one day.
Di next day, we wey be Paul companions leave, come Caesarea. We enter di house of Philip di evangelist, wey be one of di seven, stay with am.
Now this man get four virgin daughters wey dey prophesy.
As we stay there some days, one prophet wey im name na Agabus come down from Judea.

As e come to us and take Paul belt, e tie im own feet and hands, talk say, “Na so Holy Spirit talk: ‘Na so di Jews for Jerusalem go tie di man wey own this belt, and go deliver am into di hands of di Gentiles.’”
When we hear these things, both we and di people of that place beg am make e no go up to Jerusalem.
Den Paul answer, “Wetin una dey do, dey cry and dey break my heart? Because I ready no only to dey tied, but to die for Jerusalem too for di name of Lord Jesus.”
When e no gree, we stop, dey talk say, “Make Lord will happen.”
After these days we take our baggage go up to Jerusalem.
Some of di disciples from Caesarea go with us too, dey bring one Mnason of Cyprus, early disciple, wey we go lodge with.
When we reach Jerusalem, di brothers receive us gladly.
Di next day, Paul go with us to James; and all di elders dey there.
When e don greet dem, e report one by one di things wey God do among di Gentiles through im ministry.
Dem, when dem hear am, praise God. Dem talk to am say, “You see, brother, how many thousands dey among di Jews wey don believe, and dem all dey zealous for di law.
Dem don tell dem about you, say you dey teach all di Jews wey dey among di Gentiles to leave Moses, dey tell dem say make dem no circumcise dem pikin dem or waka after di customs.
So wetin? Di assembly must meet, because dem go hear say you don come.
So do wetin we tell you. We get four men wey don take vow.

Take dem, purify yourself with dem, pay dem expenses for dem, so that dem go shave dem heads. Den all go know say no truth dey for di things wey dem don tell dem about you, but say you yourself dey waka dey keep di law too.

But about di Gentiles wey believe, we don write our decision say make dem no observe any such thing, except say make dem keep demself from food wey dem offer to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.”
Den Paul take di men, and di next day purify imself go with dem enter di temple, dey declare di end of di days of purification, until dem offer di offering for each one of dem.
When di seven days almost finish, di Jews from Asia, when dem see am for di temple, stir up all di crowd and put hands on am,

dey shout, “Men of Israel, help! This na di man wey dey teach all men everywhere against di people, and di law, and this place. And e bring Greeks enter di temple too, and don make this holy place dirty!”
Because dem don see Trophimus di Ephesian with am for di city, wey dem think say Paul bring enter di temple.
All di city move, and di people run together. Dem catch Paul, drag am out of di temple. At once dem lock di doors.
As dem dey try kill am, news reach di commanding officer of di regiment say all Jerusalem dey confusion.
At once e take soldiers and centurions, run down to dem. Dem, when dem see di chief captain and di soldiers, stop to beat Paul.
Den di commanding officer come near, arrest am, command say make dem tie am with two chains. E ask who e be and wetin e do.
Some shout one thing and some another, among di crowd. As e no fit find out di truth because of di noise, e command say make dem bring am enter di barracks.
When e reach di stairs, di soldiers carry am because of di violence of di crowd;
because di crowd of di people follow behind, dey shout, “Take am away!”
As dem dey about to bring Paul enter di barracks, e talk to di commanding officer, “I fit talk to you?” E talk say, “You know Greek?
You no be di Egyptian, wey before these days stir up rebellion and lead out enter di wilderness di 4,000 men of di Assassins?”
But Paul talk say, “I be Jew, from Tarsus for Cilicia, citizen of city wey no small. I beg you, allow me to talk to di people.”
When e don give am permission, Paul, as e dey stand for di stairs, wave hand to di people. When great silence dey, e talk to dem for di Hebrew language, dey talk say,
“Brothers and papa dem, listen to di defense wey I dey make to una now.”
When dem hear say e dey talk to dem for di Hebrew language, dem quiet pass. E talk say,

“I be Jew truly, wey dem born for Tarsus of Cilicia, but dem raise me for this city for di feet of Gamaliel, dem teach me according to di strict way of di law of our papa dem, as I dey zealous for God, just as una all dey today.
I persecute this Way to death, dey tie and dey deliver both men and women enter prisons.

As di high priest and all di council of di elders testify too, from whom I receive letters to di brothers too, and I travel go Damascus to bring those wey dey there come Jerusalem for bonds to dem punish dem.
E happen to me, as I dey travel, and near Damascus, about noon, say suddenly great light shine round me from di sky.
I fall for ground, hear voice dey talk to me say, ‘Saul, Saul, why you dey persecute me?’
I answer, ‘Who you be, Lord?’ E talk to me say, ‘I be Jesus of Nazareth, wey you dey persecute.’
Di people wey dey with me see di light truly, and dem fear; but dem no understand di voice of di one wey talk to me.
I talk say, ‘Wetin I go do, Lord?’ Lord talk to me say, ‘Get up, go enter Damascus. For there dem go tell you about all things wey dem appoint for you to do.’
When I no fit see because of di glory of that light, as di people wey dey with me dey lead me by di hand, I enter Damascus.
One Ananias, devout man according to di law, wey all di Jews wey dey live there talk well about,
come meet me, stand near me talk to me say, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ For that very hour I look up for am.
E talk say, ‘Di God of our papa dem don appoint you to know im will, and to see di Righteous One, and to hear voice from im mouth.
Because you go be witness for am to all men of wetin you don see and hear.
Now why you dey wait? Get up, make dem baptize you, and wash away your sins, dey call di name of di Lord.’
E happen say when I return to Jerusalem, and while I dey pray for di temple, I fall inside trance,
and see am dey talk to me say, ‘Hurry and leave Jerusalem quick, because dem no go receive testimony about me from you.’
I talk say, ‘Lord, dem know say I put for prison and beat for every synagogue di people wey believe you.
When dem shed di blood of Stephen, your witness, I dey stand near too, dey agree with im death, and dey guard di cloaks of di people wey kill am.’
E talk to me say, ‘Go, because I go send you out far from here to di Gentiles.’”
Dem listen to am until e talk that. Den dem raise dem voice, talk say, “Remove this fellow from di earth, because e no fit make e live!”
As dem dey shout, dey throw off dem cloaks, dey throw dust for di air,
di commanding officer command say make dem bring am enter di barracks, order say make dem examine am by scourging, so that e go know for wetin crime dem dey shout against am like that.
When dem don tie am with di thongs, Paul ask di centurion wey dey stand near, “Di law allow una to scourge man wey be Roman, and dem no find am guilty?”
When di centurion hear am, e go meet di commanding officer tell am, “Watch wetin you dey about to do, because this man na Roman!”
Di commanding officer come ask am, “Tell me, you na Roman?” E talk say, “Yes.”
Di commanding officer answer, “I buy my citizenship for great price.” Paul talk say, “But dem born me Roman.”
At once di people wey dey about to examine am leave am, and di commanding officer fear too when e know say e be Roman, because e don tie am.
But di next day, as e want know di truth about why di Jews accuse am, e free am from im bonds, command di chief priests and all di council to come together, bring Paul down, set am before dem.
Paul look di council steadily, talk say, “Brothers, I don live before God with all good conscience until this day.”
Di high priest Ananias command di people wey stand near am to strike am for mouth.
Den Paul talk to am say, “God go strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit judge me according to di law, and command say make dem strike me against di law?”
Di people wey stand near talk say, “You dey insult God high priest?”
Paul talk say, “I no know, brothers, say e be high priest. Because e dey write, ‘You no go talk evil about ruler of your people.’”
But when Paul see say one part na Sadducees and di other na Pharisees, e shout for di council, “Brothers, I be Pharisee, son of Pharisees. About di hope and resurrection of di dead dem dey judge me!”
When e talk this, argument rise between di Pharisees and Sadducees, and di assembly divide.
Because di Sadducees dey talk say resurrection no dey, or angel, or spirit, but di Pharisees confess all of these.
Great noise rise, and some of di scribes for di Pharisees part stand up, argue, dey talk say, “We no find any evil for this man. But if spirit or angel don talk to am, make we no fight against God!”
When great argument rise, di commanding officer, as e fear say dem go tear Paul to pieces, command di soldiers to go down take am by force from among dem, bring am enter di barracks.
Di next night, Lord stand near am, talk say, “Take courage, Paul, because as you don testify about me for Jerusalem, so you must testify for Rome too.”
When day break, some of di Jews band together, tie demself with curse, dey talk say dem no go chop or drink until dem kill Paul.
Pass 40 people dey wey make this conspiracy.
Dem come meet di chief priests and di elders, talk say, “We don tie ourselves with great curse, to taste nothing until we kill Paul.
So now una, with di council, tell di commanding officer say make e bring am down to una tomorrow, as if una go judge im case more exactly. We ready to kill am before e near.”
But Paul sister son hear about dem ambush, come enter di barracks tell Paul.
Paul call one of di centurions, talk say, “Bring this young man to di commanding officer, because e get something to tell am.”
So e take am, bring am to di commanding officer, talk say, “Paul, di prisoner, call me ask me to bring this young man to you, wey get something to tell you.”
Di commanding officer take am by di hand, go aside, ask am privately, “Wetin you get to tell me?”
E talk say, “Di Jews don agree to ask you to bring Paul down to di council tomorrow, as if dem go inquire somewhat more accurately about am.
So no yield to dem, because pass 40 men dey wait for am, wey don tie demself with curse say dem no go chop or drink until dem kill am. Now dem ready, dey wait for di promise from you.”
So di commanding officer let di young man go, order am, “No tell anybody say you don reveal these things to me.”
E call two of di centurions come, talk say, “Prepare 200 soldiers to go reach Caesarea, with 70 horsemen, and 200 men wey carry spears, for di third hour of di night.”
E ask dem to provide animals, so that dem go put Paul on one, bring am safely to Felix di governor.
E write letter like this:
“Claudius Lysias to di most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.
Di Jews catch this man, and dem dey about to kill am, when I come with di soldiers rescue am, as I don learn say e be Roman.
As I want know di reason why dem accuse am, I bring am down to dem council.
I find say dem accuse am about questions of dem law, but no accusation wey deserve death or bonds.
When dem tell me say di Jews dey wait to attack di man, I send am to you at once, order im accusers to bring dem accusations against am before you too. Farewell.”
So di soldiers, as dem command dem, take Paul bring am for night go Antipatris.
But di next day dem leave di horsemen to go with am, and return to di barracks.
When dem reach Caesarea and deliver di letter to di governor, dem present Paul to am too.
When di governor don read am, e ask which province e come from. When e know say e come from Cilicia,
e talk say, “I go hear you fully when your accusers reach too.” E command say make dem keep am for Herod palace.
After five days, di high priest, Ananias, come down with some elders and one orator, Tertullus. Dem inform di governor against Paul.
When dem call am, Tertullus begin accuse am, dey talk say, “As by you we dey enjoy plenty quietness, and say excellent measures dey come to this nation, because of your foresight,
we accept am for all ways and for all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
But, so that I no go tire you, I beg you to bear with us and hear few words.
Because we find this man to be plague, instigator of insurrections among all di Jews through di world, and ringleader of di sect of di Nazarenes.
E even try to profane di temple, and we arrest am. We go don judge am according to our law,
but di commanding officer Lysias come pass with great violence take am away from our hands,
dey command im accusers to come to you. By examining am yourself you fit know all these things wey we accuse am of.”
Di Jews join di attack too, dey affirm say these things na so.
When di governor don wave to am to talk, Paul answer, “Because I know say you don dey judge of this nation for many years, I happily make my defense,
as you fit verify say e no pass 12 days since I go up to worship for Jerusalem.
For di temple dem no find me dey argue with anybody or dey stir up crowd, either for di synagogues or for di city.
And dem no fit prove to you di things wey dem dey accuse me of now.
But this I confess to you, say after di Way, wey dem call sect, na so I dey serve di God of our papa dem, dey believe all things wey dey according to di law, and wey dem write for di prophets;
dey get hope towards God, wey these ones imself dey look for, say resurrection of di dead go dey, both of di just and unjust.
For this I dey practice always to get conscience wey clean towards God and men.
Now after some years, I come to bring gifts for di needy to my nation, and offerings;
for which some Jews from Asia find me purified for di temple, without crowd, or turmoil.
Dem suppose dey here before you, and make accusation, if dem get anything against me.
Or make these men imself talk wetin injustice dem find inside me when I stand before di council,
unless na for this one voice, wey I shout as I stand among dem, ‘About di resurrection of di dead dem dey judge me before una today!’”
But Felix, as e get more exact knowledge about di Way, delay dem, dey talk say, “When Lysias, di commanding officer, come down, I go decide your case.”
E order di centurion say make dem keep Paul for custody, and make e get some privileges, and make dem no stop any of im friends to serve am or visit am.
But after some days, Felix come with Drusilla, im wife, wey be Jewish woman, send for Paul, hear am about di faith for Christ Jesus.
As e dey reason about righteousness, self-control, and di judgment wey dey come, Felix fear, answer, “Go your way for this time, and when e convenient for me, I go call you.”
E hope say Paul go give am money too, so that e go release am. So e dey send for am more often, dey talk with am.
But when two years don full, Porcius Festus replace Felix, and as Felix want gain favor with di Jews, Felix leave Paul for bonds.
